title_text: Why is alcohol prohibited during pregnancy?
content_text: Surely you’ve heard that alcohol and pregnancy don’t mix well. Did you know that alcohol consumption is the leading preventable cause of birth defects? Health organizations tell us that there is no known safe level of alcohol consumption during pregnancy. This is because alcohol can affect the development and growth of your baby, even in small amounts. So it’s better to be cautious and abstain completely. The FDA, for its part, has stated that drinking alcohol during pregnancy can cause serious health problems for the baby, known as fetal alcohol syndrome (FAS). FAS is a serious condition that can lead to a wide range of health issues, such as birth defects, developmental delays, behavioral problems, future learning difficulties, and behavioral challenges. If you’re pregnant, remember that alcohol consumption is not considered safe. We know it can be tempting to enjoy a glass of wine or a beer, especially on special occasions. But remember, these nine months of pregnancy are crucial for your baby’s development and future well-being. There are many ways to celebrate and enjoy without putting your baby’s health at risk.
